author: NorthEast News Desk
body: President Donald Trump said he expects the war with Iran to end after the November U.S. midterm elections and again threatened a possible attack on Pickaxe Mountain, a site associated with Iran’s nuclear program, Reuters reported early Thursday.

The statement came after Iran and the United States carried out their largest wave of attacks on shipping during the six-month conflict. Iran said it struck 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday after the United States sank five Iranian oil tankers. Reuters reported that routes through Hormuz and the Red Sea remained heavily disrupted.

Regional tensions also spread toward Saudi Arabia. Saudi civil-defense authorities issued repeated emergency alerts in Khamis Mushait as clashes with Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis intensified. The shipping attacks and wider fighting kept energy-supply concerns elevated.

Trump’s remarks described an expectation and a threat, not a newly completed strike on Pickaxe Mountain. Details about any operational decision were not announced in the Reuters report. The situation remains developing, with governments and maritime authorities assessing attacks, vessel damage and risks to commercial traffic across multiple waterways.
dek: The president said he expects the war to continue beyond the U.S. midterms and again raised a possible strike on Pickaxe Mountain.
headline: Trump threatens Iran nuclear-linked site as shipping attacks widen
